criteria.dual_build_agreement: Compile the changed tree two ways: once under the R-seed toolchain and once under the candidate toolchain. Promotion demands bit-identical bundles (bin/canlc together with the catalogue and runtime inputs) plus identical output on the combined predecessor and new-feature corpus. Concordance itself is the observation, so neither build is the oracle on its own, and any divergence vetoes promotion. Capabilities the seed-built binary cannot exercise stay outside the concordance check and are covered by pinned vectors plus bridge assumptions.
criteria.fixed_vectors: Independent human review creates every expected vector for the new bindings and behaviors (can.std.test@1 operations, http_peer operations, test_launch and dispatch semantics) directly from the written contracts: catalogue operation signatures, checker admission predicates, and emitter mappings. No build output is recorded as truth. Both the seed-built and the candidate-built binaries must replay all vectors byte-for-byte; a mismatch anywhere fails promotion.
criteria.seed_built_oracle: Compile the changed compiler and runtime using only the R-seed toolchain and its reviewed bootstrap procedure (go1.27.1, pinned inputs). That seed-built bin/canlc runs the new-feature corpus and its output originates each observation. The candidate-built binary must echo every observation byte-for-byte yet originates none. A new capability the seed-built binary cannot run drops to a hand-reviewed pinned vector, and the shortfall is named in an explicit bootstrap bridge assumption.

observation_origin.instructions: Which observation origin best accepts the R-core capability delta without letting the candidate promote itself?

state: We are promoting a changed compiler/runtime generation to R-core, the reference that will judge authoritative native Can tests. The predecessor R-seed is fixed at commit 626bf03743dbfa660d4b4651c2b0b3cceaeae0a5 with catalogue digest bdc7874222d8eccc7dc651bc949d98871e9b4e87e313b44cf1ca0c51c2957659. Since that seal, compiler/, runtime/ and tools/ moved by 231 files (+119409/-30401 lines), including compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json (+16992/-14653), runtime/catalogue.ts (+19291/-15697), the new P28 base bindings package can.std.test@1 behind $canTest, the I04 http_peer bindings behind $canHttpPeer sharing $canTest.owner, checker admission in compiler/internal/check/http_peer.go, and the new drivers compiler/internal/driver/test_launch.go, test_stage.go, test_reuse.go, test_generation_lease.go, check_json.go plus dispatch in compiler/main.go. The P06 promotion lane in tools/native-test-reference/refresh.go already fixes five gates: predecessor pin (SealIdentity must match exactly), predecessor-compatible comparison (kind kept, version advanced, each bundle delta covered by exactly one BridgeAssumption), independent new-feature observations whose producer must be the refresh seed binary and never the candidate compiler C, suite freeze (SuitePin digest and file count unchanged), and rollback identity equal to the predecessor. What remains open is where the independent new-feature observations come from for capabilities the R-seed cannot express or execute: the R-seed predates can.std.test@1, http_peer, and the test_launch/dispatch path, so it cannot run them at all. Hard constraints: no candidate self-promotion (anything produced by C as the origin of its own qualification is rejected); R-seed stays authoritative wherever it can express the behavior; every bundle delta carries exactly one bridge assumption with a human reason; P26 records the outcome in reference-core.json and evidence/P26.json with exact identities, checks, controls, cleanup and independent review.
